newsitem.title: JAPAN: Zinc prices unlikely to keep falling-Japan traders.
newsitem.headline: Zinc prices unlikely to keep falling-Japan traders.

text.p: Zinc prices will be supported above the $1,400 level in the near term, as price plunges at the London Metal Exchange (LME) overnight were a much-needed technical correction, Japanese traders said on Wednesday.
But traders said they are still worried about the volume of uncovered short positions held by Chinese smelters.
At 0730 GMT, benchmark three-month zinc was quoted at $1,490/$1,500 a tonne, against $1,480 at the Tuesday close.
"I don't think fundamentals in the zinc market are bearish. Zinc demand in the world, particulary in Europe, is still good," an trader at a major trading house said.
Another trading house trader said he believed relatively large amounts of short positions remained in the September contract, which would cause further volatility.
The traders regarded the collapse in zinc prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) overnight as a much-needed technical correction.
Three-month copper was quoted at at $2,355/$2,360 a tonne, versus $2,359 on Tuesday.
